newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says all refugees must return home.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says all refugees must return home.

text.p: Zaire on Sunday said once again that all Rwandan refugees on its soil must return home.
Interior Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda told Reuters that humanitarian corridors would be set up to help the return.
He was speaking as up to 300,000 refugees flooded home from Tanzania after the army closed the largest refugee camp there.
"All the Rwandan refugees must return home. Corridors will be created so the refugees can return to Rwanda," Kamanda said by telephone, without specifying how.
Last month, 600,000 Rwandan Hutus returned home from Zaire after Tutsi-led rebels seized control of a string of refugee towns in the east. Others fled west deeper into Zaire.
Plans for an international force to help provide humanitarian assistance to the refugees and open corridors home have been all but abandoned.
An estimated 100,000 refugees have gathered in the village of Tingi-Tingi in the east without food and proper sanitation.
Zairean authorities have stopped them heading for the regional centre of Kisangani, 250 km (150 miles) to the north west.

"The concentration of Rwandan refugees at Tingi-Tingi does not mean a new refugee camp has been set up there," Kamanda said. "Zaire has already said there will be no more new Rwandan refugee camps on its territory."
